gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the plug-in home backup sets sold by the approved battery stores have a hard 104°F ceiling. BLUETTI Apex 300 charges only at 32–104°F and runs loads only at -4–104°F, and it throws an over-temperature error above that range. That makes a Texas summer garage or patio the wrong place for it. Of the kits with an online price, only the Anker SOLIX E10 kit is rated for outdoor use (IP66) and to run at up to 131°F.
standout_why: I compared against the four cited rival pages. solarexaminer.com is the only one that gives temperature ratings, and only for installed batteries (Powerwall 3 at -4–122°F, aPower 2 at -4–131°F). It has nothing for any kit you can buy online. ocsolar.com only says the three installed systems are 'rated for outdoor installation'. homebattery.guide doesn't cover temperature, heat or garages. theenergycollective.com lists EcoFlow Delta Pro Ultra and Delta Pro 3 with Smart Home Panel 2 kits, mentions garages only in a photo caption, and doesn't cover temperature, 240 V or Anker SOLIX/BLUETTI. ChatGPT's own answer recommends a portable kit (EcoFlow DPU X) with no word on heat limits. The finding is new and decides where the kit can go, but the rivals already cover temperature for installed batteries, so it scores 2, not 3.
kit_items: Battery + inverter: Anker SOLIX E10 Power Module + 2× B6000 battery (12.288 kWh). It's the only online-priced kit I found that is rated for outdoor use (NEMA 4 / IP66) and to run at -4–131°F. It gives 7,680 W continuous at 240 V split-phase, and Anker claims it can start a 5-ton central AC (up to 155 LRA for one unit).

Whole-home transfer: Anker SOLIX Power Dock (NEMA 3R, 10-year warranty). It comes in the Automatic Backup Kit, and a licensed electrician has to connect it to the main panel. The cheaper Smart Inlet Box gives manual switchover instead.
Solar recharge for multi-day outages (optional): Anker 2× 440 W rigid panels ($999 add-on on the E10 page).

Budget alternative for indoor (air-conditioned) placement only: BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K + Home Integration Kit (5,529.6 Wh, 3,840 W, 120 and 240 V from one unit). It is capped at 104°F, so it can't live in a Texas garage in summer.
Install labor: a licensed electrician for the Power Dock or Smart Inlet Box (Anker's page says this is required). It is not in any cart.
